answer: Bridge identity to hardware: each Agent ID anchors to a TPM endorsement key burned into a chip. First, the agent generates its key inside the TPM, whose private half never leaves. Second, the TPM attests the key lives in real silicon. Third, the registry binds one ID per key and rejects duplicates. Fourth, each epoch demands a fresh quote, so a stolen key dies in hours. Forging 10,000 fakes needs 10,000 chips at $15 each, $150,000 plus two weeks of provisioning: one chip, one ID. A hollow identity is a mask with no face; a TPM-bound ID is a quill that only writes in its owner's hand.
